turns.t: Hi. I've got this itchy rash on my arms, and I think it's from the new washing powder.
Okay, let's have a look at the story. Where exactly is the rash?
Both forearms, and a bit on my neck.
How long have you had it?
Four days.
And when did you change the washing powder?
The weekend before. I bought a different brand because it was on offer.
Is the itch constant, or does it come and go?
It's worse at night. I keep scratching.
Any blisters, or any swelling of your lips or face?
No blisters. No swelling of the face, thankfully.
Have you had any trouble breathing, or wheeze?
No, nothing like that. My chest is fine.
Have you tried anything on it so far? ~
Only moisturiser. It didn't do much. ~
Let me take your pulse, temperature and oxygen level first. ~
Sure.
Pulse 76, blood pressure 122 over 78, temperature 36.7, oxygen 99 percent, breathing 16 a minute.
All normal? ~
All normal. Now let me look at your arms, please roll up your sleeves. ~
Here you go.
There are red, slightly scaly patches on both forearms and on the side of the neck, with scratch marks. No blisters.
Is it the detergent, then? ~
It looks like contact dermatitis, an irritation of the skin from something it has touched, and a new washing powder fits.
So what do I do? ~
Go back to your old washing powder, and run the clothes through an extra rinse.
Easy enough. Should I throw away the new box? ~
Keep it for now. If it doesn't settle, we may do a patch test to find out exactly what you react to.
A patch test? What's that? ~
Small patches of different substances on your back for a few days. It tells us what triggers the skin. ~
Oh, okay. I'd do that if I had to. ~
For now, I'd like to take a swab from the skin to rule out infection, if the scratching has broken it.
I think it's only scratched, not broken. ~
Then we'll not need to. But I'll keep the option, and decide next week if it is not better. ~
Fine, thank you. ~
